chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from 'Ali from Abu Basir said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who fasted in Ramadan and ate or drank unintentionally. He said, 'He completes his fast and there is no qada (making up) upon him.'
ai.seo_question: Does unintentional eating or drinking break the fast in Ramadan according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies that unintentional consumption during Ramadan does not invalidate the fast, distinguishing it from deliberate breaking. It underscores the Shia legal principle that 'nasiya' (forgetfulness) exempts one from both the penalty of kaffara and the obligation of qada, reflecting the ease (yusr) in Islamic jurisprudence.
